sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -3-  MFA No. 100953 of 2021  JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for brevity 'M.V. Act') by the appellants / claimants, calling in question the judgment and Award dated 22.01.2021 passed in MVC No.198/2019 on the file of MACT-XII, Ballari (for brevity 'Tribunal') for seeking enhancement of the compensation.

2. Brief facts leading to the case are that on 07.12.2018 at about 00.30 a.m. after loading the paddy crop in the lorry bearing registration No.KA-34/B-1503, the deceased Pakruddin being the driver of the said lorry was proceeding along with the cleaner on NH-150/a near Kodihalli gate, Challakere taluk, at that time, the driver of the offended lorry bearing Regn. No.KA-16/C-8587 came from opposite direction in high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed to the lorry of the deceased and thereby caused the accident.
As a result, the deceased sustained fatal injuries all over the body and he was shifted to Government Hospital, Challakere and later to VIMS hospital Bellary.
But he succumbed to injuries while taking treatment.

As such, a case was registered against the driver of the offending truck bearing regn. No.KA- 16/C-8587 in Crime No.173/2018 of Thalak Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 338 and 304-A of IPC.

Accordingly, a claim petition was filed by the appellants/claimants who are the legal heirs of deceased i.e. wife and children under Section 166 of MV Act, claiming compensation for the death of deceased Pakruddin.

The Tribunal after appreciating the material and evidence on record allowed the claim petition in part and awarded compensation of Rs.14,74,000/- along with interest at the rate of 7% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
The Tribunal held respondent Nos.1 and 2 jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation to the appellants/claimants.
Being aggrieved by the said award this appeal is filed by the claimants/appellants seeking enhancement of the award.

3. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for appellants/claimants and the learned counsel for respondent-Insurance Company and perused the materials on record.
4.

The learned counsel for appellants/claimants contended that the Tribunal passed the impugned judgment and award without looking into the facts and circumstances of the case and also without appreciating the evidence on record which is arbitrary and contrary to the law and facts of the case.

The learned counsel further contended that the Tribunal erred while granting the compensation in different heads, more particularly by not properly considering the nature of avocation and income of the deceased.

As such, the learned counsel prays to allow the appeal filed by appellants and prays to Smt Riyanabi W/O Late Pakruddin vs Mohammad Abbas S/O Mohammed Mustafa on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96039812/
3 enhance the compensation amount by modifying the judgment and award, passed by the Tribunal.

5. Per contra, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 i.e. Insurance company would contend that the Tribunal rightly awarded the compensation by considering the evidence on record and the Tribunal also awarded the compensation in different heads as per the settled principal of law by this Court and Hon'ble Apex Court.
Accordingly, learned counsel prays to dismiss the appeal.
6. We have bestowed our anxious consideration to the submissions made by both the parties and the evidence and materials available on record including the trial Court records, placed before us.

7. Having heard both the parties and on perusal of the records, there can be no doubt that death of the deceased Pakruddin i.e husband of the first appellant and father of appellant Nos.2 and 3 was caused in a road accident due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing regn.No.KA-16/C-8587 owned by the first respondent and insured by the second respondent.
Even otherwise, the said aspect substantiated by the documents ie. Ex.P1-the FIR, Ex.P2-the Complaint and EX.P7-the charge sheet filed by the jurisdictional Police against the offending truck.

Much less,
the said aspect is not seriously disputed by the respondents.
8. As far as the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is concerned, first appellant is the wife and appellants Nos.2 and 3 are the children of deceased Pakruddin.
The relationship of appellants with the deceased is not in dispute.
The Tribunal while awarding compensation held that deceased being self employee and was aged 45 years.
Hence, the Tribunal has taken the income of the deceased at Rs.10,000-00 per month.

However, the learned counsel for claimants has pointed out to the chart maintained by this Court which is prepared at the instance of the Karnataka State Legal Services authority which would guide the notional income to be taken at a particular year.
As per the said chart, if accident occurred in the year 2018, the notional income should be taken at Rs.11,750/- per month.
Therefore, considering the income of the deceased at Rs.10,000/- per month is on lower side and it has to be considered at Rs.11,750/- per month.

The deceased was aged about 45 years and hence future prospectus is rightly taken at 25% and since there are three dependants i.e wife and two children, the deduction should be 1/3 and multiplier applicable is 14, which works out to Rs.11750/- (Income) X 25% (future prospectus) =2937.5.
Hence, total monthly income is Rs.1750+2937.50=Rs.14687.5 9.

Thus, under the head of loss of dependency, the claimants are entitled for Rs.16,45,000/-
(14687.5 x 12 X 14X 2/3) and since there are three dependants, under the head of consortium, they are entitled for Rs.1,20,000-00 (Rs.40,000/-X3) and Rs.30,000/- is to be awarded under conventional heads.

10. Thus, the appellants / claimants are entitled for the total enhanced compensation as under:
1. Loss of dependancy 16,45,000-00 2. Loss of Consortium 1,20,000-00 Smt Riyanabi W/O Late Pakruddin vs Mohammad Abbas S/O Mohammed Mustafa on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96039812/
4 3.
Under conventional head (Towards 30,000-00 Food, Transport and attendants charges) Total 17,95,000-00 11.

Accordingly, we pass the following:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The Judgment and award dated 22.01.2021 passed in MVC No.198/2019 by the MACT- XII, Ballari is modified to the aforesaid extent.

(iii) The appellants/claimants are entitled for additional compensation of Rs. 3,25,000/-
 along with interest at the rate of 6%
 interest per annum from the date of  petition till realization.

(iv) Respondent-Insurance Company shall  deposit the additional compensation amount before the MACT-XII, Ballari in MVC - 10 - No.198/2019, within eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
(v) Registry is directed to send back the trial Court records along with certified copy of the order of this Court to trial Court forthwith.
(vi) Amount in deposit if any, before this Court be transmitted to trial Court.
(vii) No order as to costs.
